You've walked in everyone's shoes.
It was a cold, windy recess. Pip forgot a jacket, so Juniper lent hers.
I hope Pip is careful with it.
Juniper is so nice. I'm finally warm!
Brr. I wish I had a jacket like that.
Near the slide, a little kid tumbled into a puddle. Pip ran over.
Where is Pip running? I can't see from here.
Oh no, that kid is crying. I'll help them up.
Pip got there fast. Nobody else even moved.
When the bell rang, Pip gave the jacket back. One sleeve was covered in mud.
My grandma's jacket! It's ruined, and I'll have to tell her.
Uh oh. I didn't even notice the sleeve. Juniper looks so upset.
Juniper doesn't know why it's muddy. Should I say something?
Everyone stood still for a moment. Juniper had to decide what to say.
I want to yell. But I also want to know what happened.
Please don't be mad. I can explain.
This feels awkward.
My grandma gave me this jacket for my birthday. I promised her I'd take good care of it.
I slipped in the mud because I was helping a little kid who fell off the slide.
I saw the whole thing. Pip ran over to help that kid before anyone else did.
Juniper shouted and stomped inside. Pip didn't get a chance to explain.
I'm still upset, and now I feel bad for yelling too.
I wanted to say sorry, but she didn't let me.
I didn't speak up. Maybe I should have.
Pip explained about the little kid, and Otto nodded. They found wipes in the classroom.
Oh. Pip was helping someone. The mud mostly came off, too.
I'm glad she asked. I'll be more careful next time.
I'm glad I could back Pip up.
Juniper took the jacket and walked off without a word. Pip wondered all afternoon.
I'm still upset, and I don't even know what happened.
Is she mad at me? I wish I knew.
Nobody talked about it. It felt weird all day.
It was Tamsin's first day. She carried her tray into the noisy lunchroom.
So many tables. Where do I go?
Same table as always. I'll keep this spot for Wren.
Band practice is running long today.
Tamsin saw an empty seat next to Rory and walked over.
That seat is empty. Maybe they'll let me sit there.
Who's that? I don't think I know her.
I hope Rory remembers my seat.
Rory said, That seat's taken. Tamsin walked away fast.
Nobody wants me here. I should have stayed home.
Wait, was she new? I didn't mean it like that.
Here I come. I'm glad my seat is ready.
Wren sat down. Across the room, Tamsin ate alone. Rory had to decide what to do.
I'll just look at my food until lunch is over.
I kept my promise. So why do I feel bad?
Who is that sitting by herself?
At my old school I always sat with my cousin. Today I don't know anyone.
I promised Wren I'd save her a seat. She's coming late from band practice.
I asked Rory to save my seat because I get nervous walking in late.
Rory walked over and said, Sorry, that seat was saved. Want to sit with us? There's room on the end.
They weren't saying no to me. It was just a saved seat.
Keeping a promise and being kind can both happen.
Now I know someone new, too.
Rory stayed put. Tamsin ate alone and left early.
Maybe tomorrow will be better. Maybe not.
I keep thinking about her face.
Rory seems quiet. Is something wrong?
Rory whispered to Wren. Wren said, Let's both go say hi.
Two kids came over to say hi. My shoulders relaxed.
Wren made it easier to go.
I know how it feels to walk in alone.
The score was tied, one to one, with one minute left.
Stay ready. Watch the ball.
My brother is watching. We have to win!
Here comes the ball. I've got it.
Dot lost the ball. The other team kicked hard at the goal.
My glove is loose! Not now!
No, no, no! Stop it, Bea!
Oh no, that was my ball.
The ball slipped past Bea. The whistle blew. Max shouted, We lost because of you!
I tried so hard. Everyone thinks it's my fault.
We were so close. My brother saw us lose.
It started with me, not Bea. Should I say so?
The team walked off the field. Max had to decide what to say next.
I just want to go home.
I'm still mad. But was it really Bea?
If I speak up, will Max be mad at me instead?
My glove came loose right before the last kick. I tried to fix it, but there was no time.
My big brother came to watch. I really wanted to win in front of him.
I lost the ball right before that kick. That's how the other team got it.
Max kept grumbling about Bea all the way to the bus.
Maybe I shouldn't play goalie anymore.
Blaming her didn't make me feel any better.
I never said it was my ball. I feel bad.
Max stopped and said sorry. Dot said, I lost the ball first. Bea showed them her loose glove.
So it wasn't only me. I'll check my glove next time.
Losing still stinks, but we're still a team.
I'm glad I said it. It felt like a weight came off.
Max walked off alone. Nobody talked on the way to the bus.
Max is still mad at me. I'm sure of it.
I didn't really mean what I said. I just didn't say so.
Everybody went quiet. I don't like it.
